purpose: Separate CodeGraph-style bounded candidate-subgraph localization from final Prompt selection while the multi-domain knowledge base grows.

layers.candidate: Primary mechanism layer: lexical Seed IDs for R0 versus bounded local-subgraph candidate IDs for R1.
layers.prompt: Secondary consumption layer: Claim/Evidence bundles that survive selector and token budget.

decisionRules.CANDIDATE_LOCALIZATION_SIGNAL: At S50, R1 candidate recall has at least one paired required-source win, zero source/evidence losses, and candidate size stays <= 40.
decisionRules.SELECTOR_GAP: Candidate localization wins, but final Prompt recall does not improve; redesign selection/activation without enlarging Prompt by default.
decisionRules.END_TO_END_RETRIEVAL_SIGNAL: Candidate localization wins and final Prompt recall also improves without >5% average Context token increase.
decisionRules.NO_CANDIDATE_BENEFIT: R1 candidate recall has no win at any tier and no loss.
decisionRules.REGRESSION: R1 loses candidate required-source or required-evidence recall on any question.
decisionRules.ENGINEERING_SCALE_BLOCKER: Full-corpus scan work grows with corpus size; persistent lexical/source indexes and local adjacency loading are required before production-scale claims.

interpretationLimits: Stage B Gold has already been revealed, so this is a post-hoc mechanism diagnostic, not blind product evidence.
Additional roots are real multi-domain distractors; they do not add new cross-corpus semantic edges.
A candidate localization win does not authorize default Graph content in the answer Prompt.
scale-v1 is an invalid missing-Span adapter run; scale-v2 is a valid final-Prompt baseline but did not expose candidate-subgraph recall. Neither run is overwritten.
